first_steps: If the screen stays black after an update, choose "Gentoo Linux (safe graphics)" in the boot menu; it starts without the NVIDIA driver.
The NVIDIA modules are rebuilt by emerge after every kernel update (USE=dist-kernel). If an update reports that the build failed, run: emerge --ask @module-rebuild
notes: Portable install: both Intel and AMD microcode are installed.
NVIDIA proprietary driver 595 (current, open kernel modules); if it fails to build, the open nouveau driver stays in use.
The NVIDIA driver is not on the binary host: it is downloaded from download.nvidia.com and compiled on this PC, which adds several minutes and needs internet access to that address.
With 14.8 GiB of memory (and the swap), the packages that need about 4 GiB per compile job (pyside, qtwebengine, llvm, clang, webkit-gtk) get 4 compile jobs when they are built from source.
post_steps: if [ ! -f /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf ] && [ -d "/home/$1" ]; then printf "%s\n" "$2" >> "/home/$1/first-steps.txt"; chown "$1:$(id -gn "$1")" "/home/$1/first-steps.txt"; fi; exit 0

The NVIDIA driver could not be installed during the installation, so this PC runs on the open nouveau driver. To try again once the network works: emerge --ask x11-drivers/nvidia-drivers && dracut --force --regenerate-all (the driver is downloaded from download.nvidia.com and compiled on this PC).
if getent group pipewire >/dev/null; then usermod -aG pipewire "$1"; fi; exit 0

set -- /var/db/pkg/app-misc/hwmonux-*; if [ -f /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf ] && [ -d "$1" ]; then echo 'app-misc/hwmonux nvidia' > /etc/portage/package.use/installer-hwmonux-nvidia && emerge --oneshot app-misc/hwmonux || { rm -f /etc/portage/package.use/installer-hwmonux-nvidia; echo 'HWMonux NVIDIA sensors skipped'; }; fi; exit 0
